binders: m, n, q, and p are arbitrary natural numbers.
u, U, theta, gmin, and Gmin are arbitrary real numbers.
A is an arbitrary real matrix indexed by Fin m x Fin n.
B is an arbitrary real matrix indexed by Fin n x Fin q.
conclusions: narrowRange = rangeFree if and only if inputUnderflow = 0 and accumUnderflow = 0.
If inputUnderflow > 0 or accumUnderflow > 0, then rangeFree < narrowRange.
mathematical_definitions: For an r-by-s real matrix X, define rho(X) = max over i in Fin r of the sum over j in Fin s of |X(i,j)|. The maximum of an empty set and every empty sum are zero.
Define c_input = 4*(n:R)*u^(p dotminus 1)*theta^(-1)*gmin, where p dotminus 1 is truncated natural subtraction.
Define rangeFree = c_range*S, inputUnderflow = c_input*S, accumUnderflow = c_accum*S, and narrowRange = c_narrow*S.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every choice of natural dimensions m,n,q,p, real parameters u,U,theta,gmin,Gmin, and real matrices A of size m by n and B of size n by q, assume u, gmin, and Gmin are nonnegative and theta is positive. Form the product S of the maximum absolute row-sum norms of A and B, and scale the four specified coefficients by S. Then narrowRange is at least rangeFree and is exactly rangeFree plus the two underflow quantities. It equals rangeFree exactly when both underflow quantities vanish, and it is strictly larger whenever at least one of those two computed quantities is positive.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There are no positivity assumptions on m, n, q, or p; zero-dimensional matrices are allowed.
Natural subtraction is truncated: p dotminus 1 = 0 for both p=0 and p=1.
Natural powers use monoid exponentiation, so an exponent of zero gives 1, including 0^0 = 1.
The hypothesis theta>0 rules out division by zero and makes theta^(-1) positive.
U is completely unrestricted and may be negative; consequently rangeFree itself need not be nonnegative.
No ordering or scale relationship among u, U, theta, gmin, and Gmin is assumed beyond the four stated sign conditions.
If m=0 or n=0 then rho(A)=0; if n=0 or q=0 then rho(B)=0. Thus S can be zero solely because of dimensions, and it can also vanish when a matrix has zero row-sum norm.
When S=0, all four named quantities are zero, so the premise of the strict-inequality implication is false and that implication is vacuous.

The zero-characterization concerns the computed quantities inputUnderflow and accumUnderflow, not the raw parameters gmin and Gmin or their coefficients; either quantity may vanish because of zero dimensions, zero matrix norms, or zero multiplicative factors.
The strict conclusion is conditional on a computed underflow quantity being positive. Positivity of an unscaled coefficient alone does not trigger it when S=0.

The matrices enter only through the product rho(A)*rho(B). The proposition does not mention entries of the matrix product A*B, actual floating-point computations, rounding errors, or underflow events.
The parameter q affects the proposition only through the row-sum norm of B.
